checked: The summary names the content directly; the prose avoids the listed stock phrases and repeated three-sentence openings.
The General Information layout includes Core Concept, Examples, optional genuine elimination/checking shortcuts, and Traps to Watch For. No example uses a mathematical formula.

Examples progress from regime comparison to IAC/NIAC classification and riot exclusion, civilian protection, surrender/wounds and renewed fighting, weapon prohibition, proportionality and precautions, concurrent HRL/IHL assessment, emergency qualification and non-derogable rights, emergency measures/notices, peacetime duties, and peaceful resolution. These cover the distinct cases requested in the brief without number-only duplicates.
Every multistep worked solution uses numbered steps; the short one-step answers are prose. No numerical computations need display equations.

L21.note: There are no display equations to check.

checked: Teaching paragraphs contain at most three sentences; lists are limited to solution steps and compact teaching or choice lists.

L23.note: There are no illustration placeholders or figure-dependent questions.

checked: Jurisdiction is glossed in the first paragraph. IAC and NIAC precede classification cases; derogation and non-derogable precede emergency cases; hors de combat, means/methods, distinction, military objective, proportionality, incidental harm, precautions, and grave breaches are explained before use in examples.

Complementarity is explained through concurrent application and the right-to-life targeting problem. Conflict classifications use intensity and organization. Civilian and out-of-fight protections explain operation, and weapons, targeting, emergency suspension, implementation, and peacebuilding include practical application.

NIAC excludes mere riots; out-of-fight protection requires no hostile acts or escape attempt. Civilian protection has a direct-participation limit. Attacks require separate target, weapons, proportionality, and precaution checks. Article 4 teaching covers proclamation, threat to nation, necessity, nondiscrimination, notices, non-derogable protections, and ordinary limitations.
Bold introduces defined terms. Capital-letter strings are genuine institutional or legal acronyms, not emphasis; italics are not overused.
